item.description:
📚 Physics News
Multiferroics are materials that exhibit more than one prominent "ferroic" property, such as ferromagnetism and ferroelectricity. One of their most advantageous features is that they allow engineers to control their magnetic states with electric fields or vice versa, due to an effect known as magnetoelectric coupling.

item.description:

Author(s): Minghuan Zeng, Zheng Qin, Ling Qin, Shiping Feng, Lin Wu, Dong-Hui Xu, and Rui Wang Conventional altermagnetism, characterized by the even-parity spin splitting, has been intensively studied. Here, on the basis of spin-group analyses, the authors elucidate necessary conditions for the emergence of odd-parity altermagnetism. It is derived that the odd-parity altermagnetism arises from the following criteria: (i) the breaking nonmagnetic time reversal symmetry; (ii) the collinear compensated magnetism; (iii) the symmetry [ C 2 | | E ¯ ] connecting opposite-spin sublattices, where C 2 and E ¯ respectively represent a 180° rotation around the axis perpendicular to spins and the inversion separating opposite-spin sublattices. item.title: Learning quantum kernels with continuous-variable optical circuits
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Aikaterini Mandilara, Aristeides D Papadopoulos and Dimitris Syvridis
Kernel-based learning methods are central to classical machine learning, yet their quantum counterparts have largely remained limited to fixed circuit constructions. Most existing approaches aim to improve the performance of kernel-based support vector machines by heuristically tailoring kernel functions to specific tasks. In this work, we introduce a principled framework for adapting quantum kernels by translating two well-established classical techniques—the Fisher criterion and quasi-conformal kernel transformations—into the setting of continuous-variable (CV) quantum circuits. We show that the classical Fisher criterion is equivalent to maximizing the Hilbert–Schmidt distance in the quantum feature space induced by a quantum circuit.
